facts.text: StalkerDroneRL is a fully containerized ROS 2 + Gazebo project that simulates a quadcopter stalking a red ball with a Gymnasium and Stable Baselines3 deep reinforcement learning controller.
The sdrl_rl_controller package implements the Gymnasium environment and trains the drone controller with Stable Baselines3.
The project documentation says it simulates a drone in a physical environment using ROS 2 Humble and Gazebo Harmonic and that the deep RL framework is Gymnasium and Stable Baselines3.
QuadcopterTrackingEnv derives from gym.Env.

The QuadcopterTrackingEnv constructor defaults control_freq to 100, max_episode_steps to 2000 and use_sim_time to True, calls rclpy.init() when rclpy is not running and creates a node with that use_sim_time parameter.
The action space is a four-element gym.spaces.Box with low -1 and high 1 and dtype float32; the comment names the components fz, tx, ty and tz.
The observation space is an eleven-element gym.spaces.Box with low -1 and high 1 and dtype float32.
The environment subscribes to /X3/gt_odom, /X3/cmd_odom and /X3/navi_state, publishes motor speeds on /X3/ros/motor_speed and creates Trigger clients for /X3/reset_navigator and /X3/reset_dynamics.
The constant WORLD_NAME is ground_plane_world and QUADCOPTER_MODEL is lion_quadcopter, with MAX_POS_DIST 9.0 and MAX_VEL_DIST 5.0.

step converts the normalized action to motor speeds, publishes them, calls gz_client.world_control with step_multi=10 and no pause argument, waits for odometry stamped at least one control period after the step began, then computes the tracking error and reward.
_wait_for_odom polls the odometry stamp every 0.5 ms and, after 2 s of wall-clock time without a new enough stamp, logs a warning and returns normally.
gz_client.world_control sets the WorldControl pause field only when a pause argument is given, sets step and multi_step when step_multi is given, and raises RuntimeError when the request fails.
The step comments state that physics runs at 1000 Hz and control at 100 Hz and that ten physics steps are requested per environment step.

The reward configuration is base 0.2, position-distance penalty -0.0388, velocity-distance penalty -0.007, progress reward 1.0, danger-zone tilt pi/6, tilt penalty -0.5, success bonus 2.5 and crash penalty -10.0; the step reward range is documented as [-10, 10].

The reward adds the base term, the distance and velocity penalties, a progress term that is zero when the command position moved more than 0.5 since the last step, the tilt penalty above the danger-zone tilt and the success and crash terms, and clips the result to [-10, 10].
A step terminates only when the navigator state has been CRASHED for at least four consecutive steps, and truncates when step_count reaches max_steps.
step returns the normalized observation, reward, terminated, truncated and an info dict with success and crash.
reset accepts seed and options, calls super().reset(seed=seed), requests the drone reset, waits for fresh odometry, pauses physics and returns (observation, {}).
After the reset sequence, reset waits for fresh odometry on a 10 Hz node rate, measures its 5 s timeout with the node clock and raises RuntimeError when it expires.

The reset sequence pauses physics, calls the navigator reset service, publishes zero motor speeds five times, teleports the drone to random x and y with z=0.05, calls the dynamics reset service and unpauses physics.
The reset comment records that the drone is still moving slightly after being put back at the initial position and that residual velocity may need a second reset.
close shuts down rclpy when it is running, joins the spin thread and destroys the node.

The training entry refuses n_envs other than 1 because the ROS 2/Gazebo simulation exposes a single physical drone instance, and it constructs QuadcopterTrackingEnv directly rather than through gym.make.
The normalized observation is eleven float32 values: body-frame position error, body-frame velocity error, roll, pitch and body rates p, q and r.
The observation normalization constants are MAX_POS_ERR 5.0, MAX_VEL_ERR 3.0 and MAX_ANG_VEL 6.28.

action_to_wrench accepts only an action with shape (4,) and values in [-1, 1], treats action[0] as normalized force z and action[1:4] as normalized torques x, y and z, and maps them through the wrench limits.
QuadcopterParams defines a 1.5 kg mass and the diagonal inertia [0.0347563, 0.07, 0.0977].
QuadcopterParams sets hover_thrust to mass * GRAVITY * 1.1.
The project documentation notes that Gazebo shows a large initial velocity after the reset that looks like left-over velocity from the previous episode.
The training launch file starts Gazebo with gz sim -r, with the GUI or headless (-s).

determinism.notes: the fake draws its placeholder start and target from a per-instance random.Random seeded by reset(seed), so one seed and one action sequence repeat in this package; the upstream reset also calls super().reset(seed=seed) but draws its x/y jitter from the global numpy generator (train_sac.py:582-584), and its documented residual velocity is not modelled, so upstream determinism is not claimed or compared

gaps: the fake is a pure Python point-mass and attitude stand-in: it loads no Gazebo, ROS 2, quadcopter SDF, motor mixer, physics engine, contacts, sensors or navigator state machine, and was never compared with the upstream simulator

the upstream environment imports rclpy, torch, stable_baselines3 and clone modules (train_sac.py:14-39) and is never imported or run by this package; the fake only mirrors the Gymnasium methods reset, step and close and the two spaces

the action is interpreted directly as a vertical force and three torques; the upstream path goes through action_to_wrench, wrench_to_motor_speeds and Gazebo motor models, so the fake's trajectories and motor commands are not the upstream ones
the observation is a world-frame approximation of the upstream body-frame tracking error; the eleven-value layout and [-1, 1] bounds match, the values do not
the target position is a local placeholder; upstream the command pose and twist arrive on /X3/cmd_odom from the navigator and the red-ball tracker

the reward terms are copied from the upstream configuration but applied to the fake state; crash uses a local four-consecutive-step z<=0 or tilt>pi/4 test instead of the upstream /X3/navi_state CRASHED count, and success uses the initial 2.5 m curriculum radius rather than the moving curriculum

reset zeroes velocity and teleports inside the fake; upstream pauses Gazebo, calls /X3/reset_navigator and /X3/reset_dynamics, publishes zero motor speeds five times, teleports with gz_client.set_pose and unpauses, and the clone documents residual velocity after reset (train_sac.py:574-576, docs/StalkerDroneRL.md:46-54)
one environment instance is served; upstream forbids n_envs other than 1 because one Gazebo drone is shared by all environments (train_sac.py:771-779)
there is no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and only cap.world.step.v1 advances time; one tick is one 10 ms control step, the upstream ten 1 kHz physics steps are not simulated
snapshot and restore are not offered because QuadcopterTrackingEnv defines no get_state or set_state method

seeded repeats are a property of the fake only: upstream reset(seed) seeds self.np_random through super().reset, but the start x and y come from the global numpy generator (train_sac.py:582-584) and the target from the navigator and ball mover, so the seed test cases are fake-only

upstream step swallows a missing observation: _wait_for_odom returns after 2 s of wall-clock time with only a warning (train_sac.py:219-238), and step then computes reward and observation from stale odometry and reports a normal step

a live world is not lockstep by construction: the training launch starts Gazebo running (train_sac_launch.py:94-105), and step requests ten iterations with a WorldControl message whose pause field it never sets (gz_client.py:37-47, train_sac.py:393), so whether Gazebo stays paused between steps depends on gz-sim, outside the clone; the latch refuses steps but pauses nothing

the stock constructor is unsafe inside the server process: it calls the global rclpy.init and starts a daemon rclpy.spin thread, importing gz_client creates a gz-transport node at import, reset waits up to 5 s for each Trigger service and then for odometry with a timeout measured on the node clock, which is simulated time by default and never elapses while /clock is silent, and close() calls the global rclpy.shutdown and joins the spin thread without a timeout; no sim backend is declared, a live deployment needs an owned, isolated factory

in a live graph the navigator publishes its own /X3/ros/motor_speed commands at 100 Hz unless it runs in control_mode rl_train (navigator.py:241-243, 303-320, 590-607), which would compete with every step's motor command

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: Software latch only: the runtime refuses every step, reset and seed until mhs.safety.reset, so the in-process fake stops advancing and its last observation and tick stay readable; a live Gazebo world, which this package never drives, is not paused by the latch, and nothing zeroes the motor speeds last published on /X3/ros/motor_speed.
